### [`v11.28.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.0): pnpm 11.28 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.27.1...v11.28.0) pnpm 11.28.0 adds the `forceIgnoresPlatform` setting and `pnpm update --peer`, and fixes many bugs in `pnpm deploy`, `--filter`, `nodeLinker: hoisted`, and custom `modulesDir` setups. This release also carries security fixes for shell completion, bin shims on Nix, lifecycle scripts inside a custom `modulesDir`, and `userAgent` placeholders in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. ##### Minor Changes - Added the `forceIgnoresPlatform` setting. When it is `false`, `pnpm install --force` skips optional dependencies whose `os`, `cpu` or `libc` do not match the host instead of installing all of them. The default stays `true` [#​6133](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6133). ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - pnpm no longer expands environment variables in a `userAgent` set in a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. A `userAgent` with a placeholder in that file is now ignored. Before this fix, pnpm sent the variable's value to the configured registry [#​15415](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15415). - pnpm no longer treats packages inside a custom `modulesDir` as workspace projects, including one that `packageConfigs` sets for a project. Before, with a `modulesDir` such as `vendor` and a `packages` pattern such as `**`, a repeat install ran the lifecycle scripts of dependencies that `allowBuilds` had not approved [#​15412](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/15412). - On Nix, a dependency's bin named like a system utility such as `sed` can no longer redirect a POSIX bin shim or the `pnpm`, `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` launchers. The shims and launchers now ignore `node_modules` and relative `PATH` entries while they locate their own files. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules` [#​14883](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14883). - Shell completion now omits candidates containing control or invisible formatting characters, and fish completion omits names containing backslashes. Package and script names can no longer inject extra completion records or terminal escape sequences. - Commands that run pnpm again, such as `pnpm runtime set` and `pnpm env use`, no longer re-run a script that only looks like pnpm. A script named `pnpm` or `pn` that another package installed was run as though it were pnpm. - `pnpm store prune` now leaves a `dlx` cache root that is a symlink or Windows junction untouched. Cleanup no longer removes directories through that link. ##### Installing packages - `pnpm install` now fails at once when a registry or tarball server presents a TLS certificate that fails verification, such as a self-signed or expired one. The error names the certificate problem. Such requests were retried for more than a minute [#​9134](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9134). - `pnpm install` no longer appears to hang when a git dependency is fetched over SSH and ssh asks for a key passphrase or a host key confirmation. pnpm now runs ssh in batch mode, so the install fails right away with the ssh error, and a key that needs a passphrase has to be loaded into an SSH agent first. An ssh command selected through `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_SSH`, or the `core.sshCommand` git setting is kept as is [#​2227](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2227). - pnpm no longer crashes on startup when the temporary directory set by `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, or `TMP` does not exist [#​4960](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/4960). - `pnpm install --silent` no longer fails when the install is delegated to pacquet. pnpm also stops passing `-s`, `--loglevel` and the other reporting flags to pacquet [#​11936](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11936). - Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `EEXIST` when a concurrent install cleared the file or directory that was occupying a symlink path. On Windows, a symlink another process is still holding is no longer moved aside and recreated. - `pnpm install` no longer fails when writing the workspace state file encounters an error. Failures to update the state file now emit a warning instead of aborting the install [#​14550](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14550). - Installing or adding dependencies no longer fails when a previously installed local tarball file was deleted from disk [#​8367](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8367). - `pnpm install` now reads the same local tarball it installs when a dependency's absolute `file:` path contains `..`. Such a path could install a different tarball than the one it read, failing with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY`, or fail to resolve at all. - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now rejects changed local tarballs, even when the previous archive contents are in the store [#​1889](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/1889). - `pnpm add` and `pnpm install` now support installing bzip2 compressed tarballs [#​6761](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6761). - `pnpm install` now fetches committed submodules of git dependencies [#​1470](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/1470). - Interrupting `pnpm install` with Ctrl+C or SIGTERM no longer leaves a temporary lockfile (`.pnpm-lock.yaml.*.tmp`) behind in the project [#​1418](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/1418). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm run` now reinstall a single project that was moved or renamed together with its `node_modules`. Before, they reported "Already up to date" while links such as Windows junctions still pointed at the old location [#​9512](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9512). - `pnpm install` now relinks a direct dependency whose link in `node_modules` points to a missing target. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and left the broken link [#​9758](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9758). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm add` no longer skip optional dependencies that the Node.js version resolved for a `devEngines.runtime` range supports, when the range uses `onFail: download`. An explicitly set `nodeVersion` still takes priority [#​14628](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14628). - `pnpm install` now uses the running Node.js when `devEngines.runtime` declares a range without `onFail: download`. Optional dependencies supported by the active Node.js are no longer skipped [#​15230](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15230). - `pnpm install --engine-strict` now respects `engines` relaxed by `readPackage` hooks in `.pnpmfile.cjs` [#​15482](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15482). - `pnpm install` now applies changes to or removal of a global `readPackage` hook when an existing lockfile is present [#​15136](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15136). - The project's `.pnpmfile.mjs` or `.pnpmfile.cjs` now runs after the pnpmfiles of config dependency plugins [#​9891](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9891). - A `readPackage` hook that sets a dependency range to a value other than a string, such as `undefined`, now fails the install with an error that names the dependency, the package, and the pnpmfile. A guard such as `npx only-allow yarn` can stop the install before pnpm populates `node_modules` [#​3760](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/3760). - `pnpm install --prod`, `pnpm fetch --prod` and `pnpm deploy --prod` no longer install a devDependency that is only there to satisfy an optional peer dependency of a production dependency. `pnpm list`, `pnpm why`, `pnpm licenses`, `pnpm sbom` and `pnpm audit` leave it out of `--prod` results too. Issues.Title: bug(cdk/a11y): HighContrastModeDetector crashes with NG0205 when combined with withAutoCleanupInjectors()
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

### Root cause
`HighContrastModeDetector` is declared without `providedIn: 'root'`:

<link to _a11y-module-chunk.mjs HighContrastModeDetector class>

The first `inject(HighContrastModeDetector)` call from `A11yModule.constructor()` therefore creates the instance in the route-scoped injector that A11yModule is imported into (via a Material component). `withAutoCleanupInjectors()` tears down that injector on navigation. Next navigation triggers a fresh A11yModule constructor whose inject-chain references the destroyed injector → NG0205.

Fix suggestion: Add `providedIn: 'root'` to the `@Injectable` of HighContrastModeDetector (and audit the other a11y services for the same shape).

### Workaround
Add `HighContrastModeDetector` to root providers manually:
```ts
providers: [..., HighContrastModeDetector]





### Reproduction

- Angular 22.2.0, @angular/cdk 22.2.1
- `provideRouter(..., withAutoCleanupInjectors())`
- Lazy-loaded route uses any Angular Material component (MatInput, MatButton, MatDialog, ...)
- Navigate: /route-a → /route-b → /route-a  (triggers A11yModule twice)


### Expected Behavior

Navigation succeeds.




### Actual Behavior

Second visit to a route that imports A11yModule throws:
`ERROR Error: NG0205` (InjectorAlreadyDestroyed)

Stack bottoms out at `HighContrastModeDetector` factory being called in an already-destroyed route injector.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.0 (@angular/core, @angular/common, @angular/router, @angular/platform-browser, @angular/compiler-cli)
- @angular/cdk: 22.2.0 (also reproduced on 22.2.1 and 22.3.0-next.0 — unchanged a11y code)
- @angular/material: 22.2.0
- @angular/cli / @angular/build: 22.2.0
- Node: v24.15.0
- npm: 11.12.1
- TypeScript target: ES2022, moduleResolution: bundler, strict: true, strictTemplates: true
- Rendering: ZoneJS active (zoneless-compatible code via Signals)
- Browser (via Playwright): Chromium 153 (headless + headed)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (CI reproduces more frequently on Linux containers)
- Router config:
  provideRouter(
    routes,
    withComponentInputBinding(),
    withRouterConfig({ paramsInheritanceStrategy: "always" }),
    withPreloading(PreloadAllModules),
    withAutoCleanupInjectors(),
  )

Issues.Title: fix(material/form-field): measure labels independently of the outline notch
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33207

Measure the label independently of the current outline notch, then restore its inline styles. This stops truncated flex labels from expanding one pixel per resize callback when the field grows; the existing ResizeObserver scheduling stays in place.

The regression fails before the fix. Input and Select suites pass in Chromium and Firefox, including TypeScript compilation; coverage includes LTR/RTL resizing and inline style preservation. Scoped type-aware TSLint and the repository formatter pass.

Issues.Title: fix(material/sidenav): scope transitions to the nearest drawer container
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33080

An initialized outer drawer container can enable transitions on a newly rendered inner drawer through the descendant selectors. Scope the transition duration to the nearest container so nested drawers skip their initial transition and animate after their own container enables transitions.

Added a regression covering the nested drawer, content, and backdrop before and after initialization. It fails before the fix; the sidenav suites now pass in Chromium and Firefox, including TypeScript compilation. Scoped stylelint, TSLint, and the repository's staged formatter passed.

Issues.Title: docs: convert component sidenav to signals
Issues.Body:
Replaces the `async` pipe usages in `ComponentSidenav` and `ComponentNav` with signals. The breakpoints are converted using `toSignal`, which also allows the templates to be simplified.

`ComponentNav` was injecting `ActivatedRoute` to read the `section` param, because it isn't a routed component. Now `ComponentSidenav` receives the `section` param as an input through the router's component input binding and passes it down to `ComponentNav`, which loads the section's items through a `resource`. Adds a test that navigates through the routes and checks that the navigation lists the items of the section.

Also fixes the sidenav closing logic which was checking the `isScreenSmall` observable instead of its value.

Issues.Title: refactor(multiple): remove workaround for blur during change detection
Issues.Body:
`MatCheckbox` and `MatSlideToggle` were deferring marking their form control as touched to a microtask, because a focused element that gets disabled fires `blur` during change detection which used to throw a changed-after-checked error (angular/angular#17793). This is no longer the case since views that are marked for check during change detection are refreshed within the same pass and the form status classes are computed.

These changes remove the workaround and add tests that disable a focused control with Zone.js-based change detection. The existing zoneless tests already cover the same case.

Issues.Title: refactor(cdk/drag-drop): warn when the list changes while dragging
Issues.Body:
Prior to this commit, it was impossible to catch the source of this problem. While an item is dragged, its element is moved out of the list and into the body. The framework still uses that element as the anchor for the views around it. So a re-render of the list during a drag can throw, and the error comes from the renderer, which says nothing about the code that changed the list.

Steps that lead to the warning:
1) The user starts dragging an item in the list.
2) The app changes the list while the drag is still going on. For example an
   upload finishes and adds one more image.
3) The framework renders the new item and inserts it next to the dragged
   element, which is not in the list anymore. Angular then throws NG05106.

The warning is printed only in dev mode and only once per drag sequence. It names the real cause at the moment it happens, so nobody has to guess it from the renderer's error later.

The observer is created outside of the Angular zone, so it never triggers a change detection cycle.

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/menu): clear pending menu aim timeout on destroy
Issues.Body:
When the user moves towards an open submenu and stops on a sibling item, `TargetMenuAim` delays toggling the sibling's menu using a timeout. The timeout wasn't being cleared on destroy which meant that if the menu was destroyed while it was pending, the sibling's menu would still be opened afterwards.

These changes clear the timeout on destroy and remove the delay that the tests had to wait for after each test.
